title: ADU Models X, Y and Z
where: New York City. Three detached accessory dwelling units for the city's pre-approved plan library, 2025
summary: Three detached accessory dwelling units, 643 to 776 sq ft, designed for New York City's pre-approved plan library.
body: Three detached accessory dwelling units designed for New York City's pre-approved plan library, the programme that lets a homeowner build a backyard unit from a vetted design instead of commissioning a scheme from scratch. Each had to sit on an ordinary rear yard, clear zoning and energy code, and be buildable as a prefabricated lumber-framed unit.

Model X is a 643 sq ft one-bedroom on a 16 by 40 ft rectangular footprint under a single-pitch roof. Model Y turns the plan into an L, adding a walk-in closet and a dedicated office that converts to a second bedroom. Model Z stacks 776 sq ft over two floors, with a double-height living space and a bedroom and bathroom on each level, so two households can share it without sharing a bathroom.

All three run on a high-efficiency heat pump, carry insulation above NYC Energy Conservation Code minimums, and use glazing at U-factor 0.27 or lower and SHGC 0.4 or lower, compatible with Passive House and ENERGY STAR. Each plan sets aside a location for a future ADA-compliant ramp and specifies 60-minute fire-rated interior panels.
credit: Designed and drawn by me. Submitted to the city under a registered design professional of record.

title: 365 Frozen Ridge Road
where: Newburgh, New York. Interior design and documentation for a proposed single-family house, 2026
summary: Interior design, a thirty-sheet interior drawing set and client renders for a proposed single-family house in Orange County, New York.
body: A proposed single-family house on a 0.945-acre lot in Orange County. The architectural plans and elevations came from another team; I took the approved shell and designed the interiors (layouts, finishes, joinery and lighting), then produced the full interior design drawing set and the renders used to get the client to sign off.

The plan turns on a double-height living space with a plaster fireplace column at its centre, open to the kitchen and dining on one side and to the stair on the other. Thirty sheets in all: furniture and lighting layouts, HVAC and curtain-rail layouts, floor and wall tile setting-out, and elevation details for the fireplace wall, the kitchen, bedroom joinery, four bathrooms and the laundry. I also prepared the material and bill-of-quantities schedule that priced the package.
credit: Architectural plans and elevations by others. Interior design, ID drawing set, material schedule and renders by me.

title: Novo Theatre
where: Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Novo Theatre, Barishal. A 6.2-acre public science centre for the Ministry of Science & Technology. Thesis project, B.Arch final year
summary: B.Arch thesis: a 6.2-acre public science centre in Barishal, organised around a planetarium dome and a long exhibition bar.
body: A public science centre organised around a planetarium dome and a long exhibition bar. The masterplan splits the riverside site into a public arrival court, an exhibition and learning zone, and a quieter research and administration wing, so school groups and researchers can use the building at the same time without crossing paths.
Programme covers the planetarium, exhibition gallery, lecture hall, library, research lab, cafeteria, gift shop and administration.
A physical model of the site and buildings was made alongside the drawings and renders.
credit: Thesis project, B.Arch, North South University.

title: Green Farm Resort
where: Garpara, Manikganj, Bangladesh. A 6.8-acre resort masterplan built around an existing lake. In construction
summary: A 6.8-acre resort masterplan in Manikganj that keeps an existing lake at its centre, with hotel, cottages and a floating bar around its edge.
body: The plan keeps the lake as the centre of the scheme and arranges the hotel, a three-storey restaurant and conference hall, twenty rentable cottages, a floating bar, an amphitheatre and a children's playground around its edge, linked by a raised timber walkway.
I led the design and coordinated drawings through construction, including the owner's three-storey villa on the same site.
credit: Project architect: Arman H. Amir. Designed at Cornerstone Design Studio, which holds the rights to the drawings.

title: Z Commercial Complex
where: Gulshan-1, Dhaka. A 17-storey mixed-use tower on a tight corner plot. Academic project, fifth year
summary: Fifth-year studio: a 17-storey mixed-use tower on a corner plot in Gulshan-1, with an opened-up base and a covered public forecourt.
body: The lower floors are cut back and opened up to give the street a covered public forecourt and drop-off. Above it, an exhibition gallery wraps a top-lit atrium that looks down onto the forecourt, with a restaurant at the base, rentable office floors above and a gymnasium in the podium.

Upper floors step and curve at their edges, with planted terraces cut into the facade. The drawing set includes the site and ground-floor plans, floor plans from basement to roof, elevations, two full building sections, and external wall sections at roof, typical floor and basement.
credit: Academic project, B.Arch fifth year, North South University.

title: Uttara Apartment Interior
where: Uttara, Dhaka. Full fit-out of the lower floor of a duplex, in a warm beige palette. Completed 2023
summary: A full interior fit-out in Uttara, Dhaka: living room, family lounge, master bedroom, dressing area and bathroom in one warm beige palette.
body: A full interior fit-out of the lower floor of a duplex in Uttara, Dhaka, for Lithee Group. The palette of warm beige, pale marble, dark timber and brass runs through every room.

The living room centres on a marble and timber television wall. Beside the stair opening, with its black curved railing, a family lounge sits under swagged curtains and a white coffered ceiling. The master bedroom has a glazed, gridded wardrobe wall under a round cove ceiling and chandelier, and opens to a dressing area and a bathroom with a freestanding tub, a rain shower and a laundry corner.
Drawings covered furniture layouts, ceiling and lighting plans, and joinery details for each room.
credit: Project architect: Arman H. Amir. Designed at Cornerstone Design Studio, which holds the rights to the drawings.

body: A house on a narrow plot in Savar, Dhaka. The street front is a stone-clad frame filled with vertical timber louvres and recessed balconies, set against a plain white flank wall, with planting along the roof terrace.

At ground level the car parks in a tall hall beside an open timber stair, with a planted water feature at its foot. Further in, a narrow pool runs beneath the stair toward a small planted court. The cutaway shows one bedroom suite: bedroom, walk-in wardrobe and bathroom in one compact plan.

title: Gulshan-1 Apartment
where: Gulshan-1, Dhaka. Interior design for an apartment: living and dining rooms, kitchen and bedrooms
summary: An apartment in Gulshan-1 in white, warm grey and brown leather, from a moon-wall living room to the dining room, kitchen and bedrooms.
body: Interior design for an apartment in Gulshan-1, Dhaka, in white, warm grey and brown leather.

The living room is built around a large circular moon panel set beside a marble television wall with open white shelving, facing a pair of tufted leather sofas. The dining table sits between the living room and an open kitchen wall that holds the refrigerator, washing machine and glazed crockery cabinets, with linear art panels on the walls around it.

In the bedrooms, full-height lacquered wardrobes, a walnut chevron headboard wall, dressing tables with oval mirrors and a desk corner under moon-and-star wall pieces give each room its own character within the one palette.

title: Bashundhara Rooftop and Entrance
where: Bashundhara R/A, Dhaka. A rooftop terrace, ground-floor reception and front-yard garden for an existing residential building
summary: A bare rooftop turned into a residents' terrace, with a new glazed reception and planted front yard at street level, Bashundhara R/A.
body: A refurbishment of an existing residential building in Bashundhara R/A, in three parts: the bare rooftop turned into a terrace for the residents, a new reception at the foot of the stair, and a planted front yard that gives the building an address on the street.

On the roof, a timber deck under a shade-sail pergola holds the dining tables and barbecue. A flowering trellis wall dresses the stair house, a steel spiral stair climbs to the upper roof, and a dome skylight sits in a checkerboard of grey and white paving. The lighting was planned for evening use as much as for the day.

At street level the old gates and forecourt were reworked into a raised planter with a lit stone name plinth, and a glass reception box at the base of the stair. The reception and front yard have been built; the last three images are photographs of the finished work.
credit: Project architect: Arman H. Amir, ZED Architecture & Construction.

title: Jashore Apartment
where: Jashore, Bangladesh. Interior design for a family apartment: living and dining rooms, a study-bedroom and a second bedroom
summary: A family apartment in Jashore in white panelling, walnut slatted ceilings and gold trim, from the living and dining rooms to two bedrooms.
body: Interior design for a family apartment in Jashore, shown here in two parts: the living and dining spaces, and a bedroom suite.

The shared rooms are held together by white wall panelling, walnut slatted ceilings and thin gold trim. A marble and timber media wall anchors the living room; the dining table sits under a recessed ceiling with a square geometric pendant, screened from the entrance by a mirrored cabinet partition. In the study-bedroom, full-height lacquered wardrobes run alongside an open bookshelf and desk.
The second bedroom pairs a warm stone feature wall with white shaker wardrobes, a built-in entry bench with coat hooks, a dressing table with an arched mirror, and a hanging egg chair by the window.
credit: Project architect: Arman H. Amir, ZED Architecture & Construction.

title: Kazipara Apartment
where: Kazipara, Mirpur, Dhaka. Interior design for the living and dining rooms of an apartment
summary: An apartment in Kazipara, Mirpur, in dark timber and white: a living room with a hanging egg chair and a dining room under sculptural lamps.
body: Interior design for the living and dining rooms of an apartment in Kazipara, Mirpur, in dark-stained timber, white walls and soft brown upholstery.

The living room is framed by a faceted timber feature wall with a ring mirror and lit by a linear geometric chandelier; a hanging egg chair sits by the window, opposite the television wall. A gridded timber and glass partition separates it from the dining room, where an oval table runs between tall timber doors, geometric wall art and a pair of large woven disc floor lamps.

title: Wari Rooftop and Lobby
where: Wari, Old Dhaka. A rooftop terrace and entrance lobby for a residential building
summary: A rooftop terrace and a stone-clad entrance lobby for a residential building in Wari, in the dense centre of Old Dhaka.
body: A rooftop terrace and a ground-floor reception for a residential building in Wari, Old Dhaka, from the entrance the residents use every day to the roof they gather on in the evening.

The roof is laid out for use after dark. A slatted white pergola hung with trailing plants covers the dining tables and barbecue, planters line the parapet, a mesh enclosure screens the service corner, and an oval path of inset floor lights loops the open deck between the stair and water-tank houses.

Downstairs, the entrance is clad in large-format beige stone with black marble accents, with a band of rough-cut stone above the glazed reception office and a diamond-patterned feature wall at the lift lobby.
credit: Project architect: Arman H. Amir. Designed at Cornerstone Design Studio, which holds the rights to the drawings.

title: Khulna Residence
where: Khulna, Bangladesh. Interior design for a family home
summary: A family home in Khulna in white lacquer, pale marble and dark timber, from an arched living-room alcove to a long marble dining table.
body: Interior design for a family home in Khulna, in a light palette of white lacquer, pale marble and dark timber.

The living room is organised around an arched alcove lined with botanical wallpaper, with a diagonal timber bookcase and a sculptural white lounge chair; the sitting area opposite is framed by a bevelled mirror wall in dark timber and brass. A long marble dining table runs beside a glazed display kitchen, and a family lounge finishes the plan with a gallery wall and a slatted timber media unit.
credit: Project architect: Arman H. Amir, ZED Architecture & Construction.

title: Two Apartments, Dhanmondi
where: Dhanmondi, Dhaka. Living-room interiors for two apartments, the first a joint venture with Boobun – Architecture & Construction
summary: Two apartment interiors in Dhanmondi: one in warm terracotta against mural walls, a joint venture with Boobun; one quieter, in grey and white.
body: Two apartment interiors in Dhanmondi, Dhaka.

The first, a joint venture with Boobun – Architecture & Construction, is a living room in terracotta upholstery against plaster-white panelled walls, with large bird and leaf murals, a marble media wall and timber-framed folding glass doors that open the room to the dining area. A cluster of globe pendants hangs from a recessed, mirrored ceiling.
The second is quieter: grey and white throughout, with moulded wall panels, a mirrored wall that doubles the room, a sculpted timber media console and a sheer-curtained window wall.
credit: First apartment: joint venture between ZED Architecture & Construction and Boobun – Architecture & Construction; project architects Arman H. Amir and Asif Iqbal Khan. Second apartment: project architect Arman H. Amir, ZED Architecture & Construction.

title: LCLS Lawyer's Chamber
where: Gulshan-1, Dhaka. Reception and waiting area for a law chamber, a joint venture with Dreero.aec
summary: A reception and waiting room for a law chamber in Gulshan-1, under a barrel-vaulted, coffered ceiling. Joint venture with Dreero.aec.
body: Reception and waiting area for a law chamber in Gulshan-1. A barrel-vaulted ceiling with coffered ribs and cove lighting gives the long, narrow room a sense of order and draws the eye to a timber-framed window wall at its end.

The reception desk is a curved dark-timber counter with brass inlay and a black marble return, set against white walls and dark doors. Dark timber flooring, a low lounge sofa and framed landscape prints keep the waiting side calm.
credit: Joint venture between ZED Architecture & Construction and Dreero.aec – Architecture, Engineering & Construction. Project architects: Arman H. Amir (IAB AA-681) and Tanmay Hassan (IAB AH-370).

title: Uttara Residential Building
where: Uttara, Dhaka. A residential building on a narrow city plot, one three-bedroom apartment per floor
summary: A residential building on a narrow plot in Uttara, its street front composed of a white balcony frame and a dark stone frame with planted terraces.
body: A residential building on a narrow plot in Uttara, Dhaka. The street elevation is composed as interlocking frames: a white frame of stacked balconies on one side, a dark stone-clad frame with recessed, planted terraces on the other, and an open roof pavilion with a circular cut-out above.
The typical floor is a single three-bedroom apartment arranged around a central living and dining space, with the stair, lift and lobby grouped in one corner of the plan.
credit: Project architect: Arman H. Amir. Designed at Cornerstone Design Studio, which holds the rights to the drawings.

title: Green School Rooftops
where: Mohammadpur Green School, Dhaka. Two rooftops turned into outdoor play spaces for the children
summary: Two school rooftops in Mohammadpur, Dhaka, turned into fenced outdoor play spaces with swings, slides, shade canopies and soft green surfaces.
body: Two rooftop designs for Mohammadpur Green School in Dhaka, turning the flat roofs of the school into outdoor play spaces for the children, two distinct layouts with one aim.

The larger roof, about 1,526 sq ft, is a rectangle around the stair house: a green play surface edged with a blue safety border, swings, a slide, climbing frames and a round play pit, with a long planted canopy for shade. The smaller roof, about 1,026 sq ft, follows an irregular edge beside a pitched-roof section of the building, with see-saws, swings and a shaded strip along its long side. Both are enclosed by a tall mesh safety fence above the parapet.
credit: Project architect: Arman H. Amir. Designed at Cornerstone Design Studio, which holds the rights to the drawings.

title: Noubahini School Library
where: Bangladesh Noubahini School and College, Chattogram. A library for the school, planned as four connected rooms
summary: A library for Bangladesh Noubahini School and College in Chattogram: four connected rooms for reading, group work and presentations.
body: A library design for Bangladesh Noubahini School and College in Chattogram, planned as four rooms within one rectangular floor so that quiet reading, group work and presentations each have their own space.

One room is given to long reading tables. Another holds a green, branching shelf-and-bench island with hexagonal stools for younger readers. A third contains the issue desk and stacks, and the fourth is a projection area with curved built-in seating around a round table. Timber shelving lines the perimeter walls throughout.
credit: Project architect: Arman H. Amir. Designed at Cornerstone Design Studio, which holds the rights to the drawings.

title: Narayanganj Kitchen
where: College Road, Narayanganj. A kitchen remodel for an apartment
summary: A kitchen remodel in Narayanganj: cream lacquer cabinets, black stone worktops, a patterned tile backsplash and new lighting, drawn wall by wall.
body: A kitchen remodel for an apartment on College Road, Narayanganj. New cream lacquer cabinets and open shelving, black stone worktops and a patterned tile backsplash were fitted to the existing room, with a tall pantry and appliance unit and under-cabinet lighting along the worktop.
The renders are sectional views through the room, one for each wall, used to check the cabinet runs, the appliances and the door and window positions together.
credit: Project architect: Arman H. Amir, ZED Architecture & Construction.
